chunks: As for what Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Barqi, from al-Marzuban ibn ʿImran, from ʿUmar ibn Yazid, who said:

I said to Abī ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام: I get up when dawn has already risen. If I begin with the fajr prayer, I perform it at the beginning of its time; but if I begin with salat al-layl and the witr, I perform the fajr prayer in the time of those ones. He said: Begin with salat al-layl and the witr, but do not make that a habit.

key_terms.أَوَّلِ وَقْتِهَا: the earliest part of the prayer’s prescribed time
key_terms.ابْدَأْ: begin first; an instruction giving order of performance
key_terms.الْفَجْرُ: the dawn time marking the beginning of the fajr prayer time
key_terms.الْوِتْرِ: the concluding unit of the night prayer
key_terms.صَلَاةِ اللَّيْلِ: the recommended night prayer performed before fajr
key_terms.عَادَةً: a regular practice or habitual pattern

ai.seo_question: If dawn has risen, should I pray salat al-layl and witr first or begin with fajr?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the case of one who rises at dawn and must choose between immediately performing fajr or first completing salat al-layl and al-witr. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام instructs beginning with the night prayer and witr in that circumstance, while warning that this should not be turned into a regular habit.
